correctness.rationale: Exact trace gain is (A²)ii/Aii. The beta=1 expectation is tr(A²)/tr(A); uniform expectation is bounded by the top eigenvalue via the Rayleigh quotient. Cauchy–Schwarz over r−1 remaining eigenvalues and one-variable maximization yield the exact factor (1+sqrt(r))/2. A block Gram family approaches equality for every rank r; an explicit three-coordinate example and the 2x2 identity settle minimal dimension. For every fixed real beta>1, a second block family has uniform gain asymptotic to T and beta-weighted gain tending to one. All quantifiers and rank/positive-diagonal boundaries are stated. Standalone exact-rational checker executed successfully; numerical checks only corroborate, they do not prove infinite claims.

value.rationale: The Gibbs pivot powers are an actual numerical-algorithm design choice; the quantitative question whether more diagonal exploitation improves immediate approximation quality is motivated directly by the cited methods. The exact rank-r supremum measures the largest possible penalty of the canonical rule relative to exploratory uniform sampling, and a minimal 3x3 counterexample makes the limitation concrete. The complete beta>1 rank-two divergence identifies a substantive qualitative loss of robustness; the answer is not a renaming or arbitrary data slice and is useful for selecting or safeguarding pivot powers.
